title: model catalog: add capability filters, compatibility flags, and pricing/limits to model listing endpoints (OpenAI compatibility)
author: Ava Martinez
release_notes: Adds capability filters and compatibility flags to the model listing API; surfaces per-model pricing and token limits; SDK and docs updates. Backwards-compatible (additive fields).
description:
Context: The model catalog listing endpoints only returned basic metadata, which forced consumers to maintain separate mappings for capabilities, OpenAI-compatibility, and pricing. This made SDKs and routing logic brittle and led to inconsistencies between hosted and OpenAI-compatible endpoints.

Motivation: Provide a single, canonical surface for model capability discovery so routing, pricing estimation, and SDKs can rely on stable fields.

What this PR does:
- Adds new response fields to GET /api/v1/models and the internal model registry endpoint: 'capabilities' (list of strings, e.g. ["chat","streaming","function_calling"]), 'compatibility_flags' (array of strings to indicate compatibility layers, e.g. ["openai_compatible"]), flattened pricing fields (price_per_1k_tokens_usd, price_per_embedding_usd) and token limits (max_input_tokens, max_output_tokens, recommended_batch_size).
- Adds query filters on the list endpoint: ?capability=chat,?openai_compatible=true,?min_max_output_tokens=1024 and support for multiple capability filters.
- Keeps existing fields for backward compatibility; clients are encouraged to prefer the new fields.
- Adds unit and integration tests for the new filters and serialized fields.
- Updates SDK typings and the model catalog docs page with examples, plus a small console enhancement to show pricing and flags.

Implementation notes:
- API surface changes are additive; the response shape extends the existing model DTO.
- A lightweight DB migration adds/normalizes model_metadata JSON for legacy entries.
- The compatibility flag is represented in responses as an array of strings to avoid nested objects in the public API.

Checklist:
- [x] API schema + handlers
- [x] DB migration
- [x] SDK typings (python/typescript)
- [x] Docs + changelog
- [x] Unit + integration tests
- [x] Observability: added metrics for filter hit rates

Follow-ups:
- Wire pricing to the billing estimator (ENG-4292)
- Expose model capability subsets in the console filters (PM-318)
